newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Shi'ites say cleric arrested.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Shi'ites say cleric arrested.

text.p: A group of Saudi Arabian Shi'ite Moslem clergymen said on Wednesday Riyadh had arrested a leading Shi'ite cleric and called on the kingdom to release hundreds of political prisoners.
The Grouping of Clergymen of Hijaz said in a fax to an international news agency that state security forces on Tuesday "detained in a terrorist fashion" Hashem Mohammed al-Shakhsi.
The previously unknown group said the arrest was carried out in al-Ihsa'a, in eastern Saudi Arabia where many of the country's minority Shi'ites live.
The statement also accused Saudi Arabia's Sunni Moslem rulers of detaining Shakhsi, 39, a few years ago and "exposing him to all sorts of torture".
The group called on fellow clergymen in Saudi Arabia and in the Moslem world and human rights groups to move swiftly to seek the release of Shakhsi and other political prisoners.

"We also remind that dozens of clergymen and honourable people from all over the country are still detained in addition to hundreds of university youths and intellectuals and others," the statement said.
It also listed the names of 23 Shi'ite clergymen who it said were being held by Saudi authorities.
The group said it had sent the statement to foreign missions in the kingdom, the cabinet, the Royal Court, various ministries and Saudi Moslem authorities.
